context: A police officer briefs on factory safety
purpose: Teach: 晋/炉/包装/試みる/封筒/簡素/直結/軽視

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 晋さんの工場、電気炉の検査記録、共有頂きました。
lines.en: We've received the inspection records from Shin's plant—the electric furnace documentation.
lines.style: Professional, measured opening. Clear enunciation on the technical terms. Steady eye contact. No rush. The tone of someone who has reviewed the paperwork and is proceeding with the next step.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。包装ラインの安全策、試みる新指針もあります。
lines.en: Yes. We're also implementing a new safety protocol for the packaging line.
lines.style: Attentive and engaged. Slight forward lean—showing willingness to align. Calm delivery, deliberate pacing on "packaging line" to confirm understanding. Cooperative without sounding obsequious.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 郵送はやめ、警察封筒で直接届けてください。
lines.en: Stop using the mail. Deliver it directly in official police envelopes.
lines.style: Shift to directive authority. Crisp, businesslike tempo. No apology in the phrasing—this is instruction, not suggestion. Brief pause before "directly" for emphasis. Professional distance maintained.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 簡素なフォーマット、警察システムに直結させて運用します。
lines.en: We'll use a simpler format and integrate it directly with our police database.
lines.style: Assured and responsive. Confident nod in the voice—showing he's already thinking through the logistics. Clear articulation on "police database." Not defensive, just competent confirmation.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 安全を軽視しないで、お願いします。
lines.en: Please don't underestimate the importance of safety here.
lines.style: Firm closing statement. Weight on "safety." Slower pace, deliberate. The politeness of "please" doesn't soften the resolve—it grounds the gravity. Slight lean forward. This is not negotiable.
